cover.tagline: Connecting services, data and AI into measurable impact.
cover.caption: Alameen Technologies — since 2008, 86 organizations run on our systems.

company.title: Alameen Technologies
company.tagline: Over fifteen years building software and GIS systems for municipalities, institutions and government bodies across Palestine and the Middle East.
company.caption: A strategic partner, not a technology vendor.
company.b1: To be the first technology choice for e-governance and digital transformation.
company.b2: Innovative technologies that serve society's needs and support its growth.
company.b3: A national digital infrastructure that elevates government and service performance.
company.b4: Strategic partnerships built on trust, quality and continuous development.

reach.title: Who we serve
reach.tagline: Eighty-six organizations run on our systems — from ministries to municipalities to universities — since the company was founded in 2008.
reach.caption: Figures drawn from our actual client register.
reach.b1: 13 ministries and government authorities — Water, Land, Education, Finance, Social Affairs, Transport.
reach.b2: 54 municipalities and local bodies across the governorates.
reach.b3: 7 international funders and partners: World Bank, USAID, GIZ, Global Communities, Tetra Tech, BTC.
reach.b5: More than a thousand schools served by the interactive educational atlas.

coverage.title: Where our systems run

coverage.caption: 57 live deployment sites on the map of Palestine.

coverage.b4: And the water sector nationally, as far as the Coastal Municipalities Water Utility in Gaza.

projects.tagline: Systems delivered and running, funded and supervised by the World Bank, USAID, GIZ and the Municipal Development and Lending Fund.
projects.caption: Projects delivered, not proposals.

projects.b2: Citizen service centers across 30 municipalities — MDLF.
projects.b3: E-services for Al-Bireh, Tulkarem, Jericho and Bethlehem — USAID-funded.

specializations.title: What we do well
specializations.tagline: Eight lines of work, each proven by a system running today at a real organization — not a list of intentions.
specializations.caption: Every specialization has a delivered system behind it.
specializations.b1: Full enterprise systems, from the database to the screen.
specializations.b2: Geographic information systems: maps, layers and spatial analysis.
specializations.b3: Applied AI governed by permissions — not a laboratory experiment.
specializations.b4: E-services portals for citizens and staff, and digital archiving.

stack.title: What we build on today
stack.tagline: Currently supported versions, not inherited ones: .NET 10, React 19, PostgreSQL 18 — all containerized and deployed into your infrastructure.
stack.caption: The same stack running the national water platform.
stack.b1: Current supported versions, so you do not buy a system born obsolete.
stack.b2: PostGIS puts geography in the database itself, with no separate map server.
stack.b3: Docker containers deploy to your servers or your cloud — no vendor lock-in.
stack.b4: REST APIs documented with OpenAPI, so integration with your existing systems is direct.

partners.title: Our technology partners
partners.tagline: We build on established global platforms and deliver regionally through a local partner in the Gulf market.
partners.caption: Working technology partnerships, not logos on a slide.
partners.b3: DocuWare and OpenKM — document management and digital archiving.
partners.b5: UTTS Group — Oman, our partner in the Gulf market.

ecosystem.title: Six domains. One connected platform.
ecosystem.tagline: One identity, shared data, and capabilities that serve every domain.
ecosystem.caption: From service to decision — everything connected.
ecosystem.b1: One sign-in and one permission model across every domain.
ecosystem.b2: Data is read once, so the indicator, the map and the report share a source.
ecosystem.b3: Adding a domain is assembly on the platform, not a project from zero.

capabilities.title: Technology that makes the transformation smarter
capabilities.tagline: What the six domains share: nine capabilities built into the platform rather than bolted onto it.
capabilities.caption: The same capabilities serve every domain.
capabilities.b2: What is built for one domain is available to the rest at once.
capabilities.b3: Documented REST interfaces, so integrating with your existing systems is a known path.

aiAssistant.title: Ask your operational data
aiAssistant.tagline: A question in plain language, answered from this organization's own data — not from general knowledge and not from a model trained on someone else's.
aiAssistant.caption: Sabr, the assistant, inside the platform.
aiAssistant.b1: Ask in Arabic or English — no special phrasing, no query language.
aiAssistant.b2: The answer carries the real table it came from, not a bare number.
aiAssistant.b3: It works inside the asker's own permissions — it sees what they see, no more.

aiAnswers.title: One assistant, every shape of answer
aiAnswers.tagline: A single answer becomes a table, a chart or a printed document — the user picks the shape, not the model.
aiAnswers.caption: Switch the shape of a result without asking again.
aiAnswers.b1: Table, bars, pie, line — switched instantly, with no new question.
aiAnswers.b2: Official letterheaded printing from any result.
aiAnswers.b3: Excel export with correct Arabic ordering.

aiMap.title: The answer on the map
aiMap.tagline: A question about assets that have a location is answered spatially: the result is drawn on the map instead of staying as rows.
aiMap.caption: Well density across the governorates, from one question.
aiMap.b1: Located assets are drawn on the map automatically.
aiMap.b2: Heat maps and geographic centroids from the same question.
aiMap.b3: The true count and the records without a location are stated, so a partial map is never read as a whole one.

aiSafety.title: The model never reaches the database
aiSafety.tagline: No connection string, no SQL, not one table name — the assistant asks the governed reporting engine with the asking user’s own token.
aiSafety.caption: The first question a government client asks, answered by design rather than by promise.
aiSafety.b1: Every call carries the asker's permissions: a dataset they cannot read is not in the catalog, and a column they cannot read is refused by the endpoint.
aiSafety.b2: Tenant isolation and row-level limits apply on the same path a human report run takes.
aiSafety.b3: Results are aggregated and capped by us, not by the model — no table dumps.
aiSafety.b4: Metadata travels with every result: the filters, the column units, and the true row count.

aiReport.title: From answer to owned report
aiReport.tagline: A result worth keeping is saved as your organization's report — opened, edited and shared, rather than trapped in a conversation.
aiReport.caption: Saving a result as a report that opens in the builder.
aiReport.b1: Any result becomes a saved report in one click.
aiReport.b2: It opens in the report builder to be edited by hand.
aiReport.b3: It inherits its dataset permissions, so sharing cannot leak it.

aiReportBuilder.title: Describe it — it builds itself
aiReportBuilder.tagline: Describe the report in a sentence and a full draft arrives — columns, filters and grouping — editable rather than imposed.
aiReportBuilder.caption: A report drafted from plain language.
aiReportBuilder.b1: Columns, filters and grouping proposed from the description.
aiReportBuilder.b2: The user edits and approves — the decision stays with them.
aiReportBuilder.b3: Datasets are whitelisted and governed, so no source is invented.

aiDashboard.title: The same engine, on the dashboard
aiDashboard.tagline: A dashboard is a grid of tiles, each a saved report with its own permissions and filters — not a screen a developer had to write.
aiDashboard.caption: A dashboard composed from saved reports.
aiDashboard.b1: Every tile is a saved report, with its own permissions.
aiDashboard.b2: Set the period once and every tile follows it.
aiDashboard.b3: A dashboard is data, not code: copied to another organization with no release.

aiDashboardBuild.title: Describe the dashboard — watch it build
aiDashboardBuild.tagline: Write what you want to see and the dashboard assembles in front of you, tile by tile — then you arrange it by hand.
aiDashboardBuild.caption: A dashboard generated from one description.
aiDashboardBuild.b1: One sentence produces a proposed grid of tiles.
aiDashboardBuild.b2: Reorder, remove and add by dragging.
aiDashboardBuild.b3: Saved and shared like any dashboard, and still editable.

workflow.title: Stages, SLAs and owners
workflow.tagline: Every request moves along a configured path: stages, response times and a named owner per step — defined by configuration, not code.
workflow.caption: The path is drawn in front of you, and each route carries its rules.
workflow.b1: Stages with SLA timers and a defined owner for each step.
workflow.b2: The path is drawn as a diagram — click any route to see the condition that opens it.
workflow.b3: Not one path but a library of them, one per request type.
workflow.b4: Every decision is recorded with its author and time, so the path is auditable rather than assumed.
workflow.b5: Changing a path is configuration that takes effect immediately, not a new release.

services.title: One service definition, one rendering engine
services.tagline: A service is defined once — its fields, outputs, fees and path — and then rendered the same way wherever it is received.
services.caption: From service definition to a tracked request.
services.b1: A no-code form builder: fields, validation and conditions by configuration.
services.b2: A service carries its outputs, its fees and its form in one definition.
services.b3: A request is tracked from submission to completion on one register.
services.b4: The same renderer builds the screen in every module that receives the service.
services.b5: The handling module adds only its own fields; the rest is shared.

documents.title: A document that cannot be edited once issued
documents.tagline: A licence or certificate is a signed snapshot produced by the step that granted it — never edited afterwards, corrected by revoking and re-issuing.
documents.caption: The document previewed before issuing, then the signed copy.
documents.b1: Preview the document at real page size before it is issued.
documents.b2: What is issued is frozen: re-rendering it from today\u2019s data would defeat the point.
documents.b3: A printed QR opens a public verification page with no sign-in.
documents.b4: Revoke and re-issue is the correction path, never an edit to what was issued.

geo.title: No record without geography
geo.tagline: Location is not a separate screen: every asset and every request carries its own, and the map is one layer over all the modules.
geo.caption: Infrastructure and resources, on the same map.
geo.b1: Every module's assets on one map, each layer declaring its source.
geo.b2: Import the geometry instead of redrawing it by hand.
geo.b3: Shapefile and GeoJSON both, for import and export — never a single format.
geo.b4: Layers are granted to roles, so a role sees only what belongs to it.

notifications.title: What is sent, and when
notifications.tagline: A notification is configured, not coded: choose the event, the recipient, the channel and the text, and it fires on its own.
notifications.caption: The event happens, and the platform reacts at once.
notifications.b1: Event, recipient, channel and text are all configuration, not code.
notifications.b2: The notification fires automatically the moment the state changes.
notifications.b3: An in-platform inbox alongside email and SMS.
notifications.b4: Every notification links back to the record that raised it.
